newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai oil upgrading plant hit by debt - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dubai oil upgrading plant hit by debt - paper.

text.p: Operations at a waste oil recycling plant in the Gulf Arab emirate of Dubai have been restricted because of debts run up by the refinery's Indian owners, the UAE Gulf News newspaper reported on Friday.

Western Oil Co, part of India's Gadgil Western Corp, had run up a debt of over ten million UAE dirhams ($2.7 million) since the plant, originally intended as a 125,000 tonnes a year fuel oil upgrading refinery, started in 1995, the paper said.

The fuel oil refinery, which was planned to export gasoline, middle distillates and bunker fuels, was converted into a waste oil recycling plant last year after the project suffered from technical and marketing problems.
"Operations are severely cramped by the unavailability of enough quantities of the base stock, i.e. waste fuel," an unnamed senior official at the plant told Gulf News.
The plant, at Dubai's Jebel Ali free trade zone, had been running 150 tonnes of waste oil a day in recent months, the paper said.
A bank was studying proposals to revive the cash-strapped plant including the release of capital to keep it operational.

"A bank has initiated some steps to corrrect the financial position of the company, including an agreement in principle to free funds for short term capital needs. But nothing definite has yet emerged," a source at Western Oil told Gulf News.
Gadgil's Jebel Ali fuel oil refinery was one of the first privately-backed refinery projects in the United Arab Emirates.
